fields.home.hero.sub: Edit headlines, CTAs, and copy directly on the page. Vercel redeploys automatically on publish.
fields.cta.label: Start today
fields.cta.title: One command away from a live editor.
fields.cta.sub: Your marketing team won't need to open a code editor just to change a headline. Give them the power to edit, safely.
fields.features.label: What you get
fields.features.title: Everything you need. Nothing you don't.
fields.features.sub: Built for developers who want to hand editing control to their clients, without handing over their codebase.
fields.features.f0.title: Magic link auth
fields.features.f0.body: Email-only login with short-lived signed tokens. No passwords, no OAuth config. HTTP-only cookies for sessions.
fields.features.f1.title: In-page editing
fields.features.f1.body: Green outlines on hover. Click to open an inline editor. Live preview of changes before publishing.
fields.features.f2.title: GitHub → Vercel
fields.features.f2.body: Publishing commits content.json to your repo. Vercel detects the push and redeploys. Zero extra infra.
fields.features.f3.title: Roles & access
fields.features.f3.body: Owners publish. Editors save drafts. Add team members via env vars. No database required.
fields.features.f4.title: Secure by default
fields.features.f4.body: Origin validation, rate limiting, field ID allowlists, content sanitization. Plain text only, no arbitrary HTML.
fields.features.f5.title: Zero dependencies
fields.features.f5.body: No CMS subscription. No hosted service. No vendor lock-in. Just an npm package and your existing Vercel project.
fields.hiw.label: How it works
fields.hiw.title: Up and running in minutes.
fields.hiw.sub: Six steps from install to live editing. No database, no third-party CMS, no pipeline changes.
fields.hiw.s0.title: Install the package
fields.hiw.s0.body: Run one command to install and scaffold. The CLI creates the API routes and config file automatically. Nothing to build from scratch.
fields.hiw.s1.title: Mark editable content
fields.hiw.s1.body: Wrap any headline, paragraph, or link with EditableText. Keep your existing className and styles. EditLayer wraps around them, never rewrites them.
fields.hiw.s2.title: Set env vars & deploy
fields.hiw.s2.body: Add your secret, site URL, Resend API key, and GitHub token to Vercel. Push to GitHub. That's the entire backend.
fields.hiw.s3.title: Open edit mode
fields.hiw.s3.body: Visit yoursite.com/?edit=true. Enter your email, click the magic link. Green outlines appear on every editable field immediately.
fields.hiw.s4.title: Click, type, publish
fields.hiw.s4.body: Click any field to edit inline. See the live preview as you type. Save a draft to share, or hit Publish to commit directly to GitHub.
fields.hiw.s5.title: Vercel redeploys
fields.hiw.s5.body: Publishing writes editlayer/content.json to your repo via the GitHub API. Vercel detects the commit and redeploys automatically.
fields.setup.label: Setup guide
fields.setup.title: From zero to editable in under 5 minutes
fields.setup.sub: Copy, paste, deploy. Every command and env var you need. Nothing more.
fields.faq.label: FAQ
fields.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
fields.faq.sub: Everything you need to know before installing.
fields.faq.q0.a: No. EditLayer is a thin editing layer that sits on top of your existing Next.js app. There's no external service, no dashboard, and no content schema. Your content lives in a JSON file committed directly to your GitHub repo.
fields.faq.q1.q: Where does my content get stored?
fields.faq.q1.a: In editlayer/content.json inside your own GitHub repository. When you publish, EditLayer commits the file via the GitHub API. Vercel detects the commit and redeploys automatically. You own everything.
fields.faq.q2.q: What if an editor breaks the site?
fields.faq.q2.a: Editors can only save drafts. They can't publish. Only owners (set via env vars) can push changes live. Every publish is a real git commit, so you can always revert via GitHub if something goes wrong.
fields.faq.q3.q: Do I need a database or server?
fields.faq.q3.a: No. There is zero infrastructure to run. All state lives in your GitHub repo. The only services you need are already part of your stack: Next.js, Vercel, and GitHub.
fields.faq.q4.a: EditLayer supports Next.js 13+ with the App Router. It uses React Server Components for content loading and client components for the editing UI. Pages Router is not currently supported.
fields.faq.q5.q: Is it free? What's the license?
fields.faq.q5.a: EditLayer is MIT licensed and completely free, forever. It's self-hosted, so there's no subscription, no usage cap, and no vendor lock-in.
fields.faq.q6.q: How is this different from a headless CMS?
fields.faq.q6.a: A headless CMS requires a separate service, schema setup, and often a monthly fee. EditLayer requires none of that. Your site is the editor: marketers edit copy directly on the live page, changes deploy via your existing Vercel pipeline.
